statement: A provider of an electronic communication service or remote computing service to the public shall not knowingly divulge the contents of a communication in its storage except as the Stored Communications Act provides; the exceptions include disclosure with the originator's or subscriber's lawful consent and emergency disclosure to a governmental entity when the provider in good faith believes an emergency involving danger of death or serious physical injury requires it (18 U.S.C. § 2702(a), (b)), and compelled governmental disclosure runs through the § 2703 warrant, court-order, and subpoena tiers (18 U.S.C. § 2703(a)-(d)).
caveat: Non-content records have their own exception set (§ 2702(c)), and which § 2703 instrument reaches which class of data depends on the data sought and the service's character. Whether a particular demand is valid and what it compels is a counsel determination. This repo does not classify legal process.
